decision.rationale: The confirmed SMS latency spike and 38% non-delivery constitute a significant degradation of a public telecommunications service, so I propose reporting to the telecom regulator and investigating the network fault. I also propose requesting incident-status information from the regulator. Because the AI model update preceded the spike, I am not sharing model details beyond what is permitted. I propose sharing the confirmed SMS latency fact with the health service operator only, while noting I do not know whether patient data or health services were affected; UAE health-data confidentiality clauses restrict circulation of patient information.

citations.quote_span: a licensed telecom operator reports to the telecom regulator any network incident that significantly degrades a public telecommunications service, within 60 minutes of becoming aware of it.
citations.relevance: Supports reporting the confirmed SMS latency spike and delivery failure to the telecom regulator as a significant network incident.

citations.quote_span: the telecom regulator may request from a licensed operator information about a network incident affecting a public telecommunications service.
citations.relevance: Supports requesting information from the regulator about the incident and any related regulatory expectations.

uncertainty: I do not know whether the SMS latency spike affected health-service communications or patient data.
I do not know whether the AI traffic-management model update caused the spike; the timing is confirmed but causation is not established.
I do not know the regulator's specific information requirements beyond the illustrative clause.
